title: 做選擇與安排時間
subtitle: Choosing, rules you must follow, and sequencing your day

vocab.gloss: to decide (to do something); to resolve; decision

example.pinyin: Wǒmen juédìng zhōumò qù Táiběi wán.

grammar.title: 還是 in questions, 或者 in statements
grammar.pattern: A 還是 B？（問句） ／ A 或者 B（說明）
grammar.explanation: When you ask someone to pick between two things, use 還是: 你要吃麵還是吃飯？ When you are not asking a question, but just saying that either one is possible, use 或者: 我們搭捷運或者走路都可以。 So 還是 belongs to choice questions, and 或者 belongs to statements about open possibilities. Both can follow words like 決定, 選擇 and 需要: 我還沒決定要去看電影或者去逛夜市。
grammar.contrast: 還是 vs 或者: both mean "or", but the sentence type decides. If there is a question mark and you want the other person to choose one, use 還是. If you are telling, not asking, use 或者. (Note 還是 also means "still", as in 我還是不知道。)
grammar.common_error: Learners say 你要喝咖啡或者茶？ using 或者 in a choice question. In a question offering two options it must be 還是: 你要喝咖啡還是茶？

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī miàn háishì chī fàn?
examples.gloss: Do you want noodles or rice?

examples.hanzi: 週末我想去逛書店或者看電影。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng qù guàng shūdiàn huòzhě kàn diànyǐng.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào xiànzài juédìng háishì míngtiān gàosù wǒ?
examples.gloss: Do you want to decide now or tell me tomorrow?

passage.title: 選哪一個？
passage.hanzi: 我很不會做決定。昨天下班以後，朋友問我要喝珍珠奶茶還是咖啡，我想了半天。店裡的飲料選擇太多了，我真的需要時間。朋友笑著說：「珍珠奶茶或者咖啡都很好喝，你別想太多。這也是一個學習決定的機會啊！」最後我決定買一杯珍珠奶茶，也給朋友買了咖啡。
passage.gloss: I'm really bad at making decisions. Yesterday after work, a friend asked me whether I wanted bubble tea or coffee, and I thought about it forever. The shop had too many drink choices — I really needed time. My friend laughed and said, "Bubble tea or coffee, both taste great. Don't overthink it. This is also a chance to practise deciding!" In the end I decided to buy a bubble tea, and I bought my friend a coffee too.

example.gloss: There are lots of people on the weekend; you definitely have to go earlier.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ yǒu yìbǎi kuài, bù néng mǎi nàge.
example.gloss: I only have a hundred dollars, I can't buy that.

grammar.title: 應該／必須／一定要：three levels of "must"
grammar.pattern: Subject + 應該／必須／一定要 + Verb Phrase
grammar.explanation: 應該 is advice or expectation — "ought to, should" (the speaker thinks it is the right thing, but you can still say no). 必須 is a rule or hard requirement, common in written notices and formal speech (school, company, 捷運). 一定要 is the everyday spoken way to say "really must", used for strong advice or emphasis; it is far more common in daily Taiwan conversation than 必須. 一定 can also stand alone before a verb to mean "surely": 他一定會來。
grammar.contrast: 必須 vs 一定要: both mean "must", but 必須 states an outside rule (郵局的要求), while 一定要 expresses the speaker's own insistence or emphasis. If a sign or a boss imposes it, use 必須; if you are urging a friend, use 一定要. 應該 is weaker than both — it leaves room for choice.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 必須要 (doubling the "must") and negate it as 不必須. 必須 already contains "must", so drop the 要; and for the negative use 不用 or 不必 (你不用寫電話), never 不必須.

examples.hanzi: 你感冒了，應該去看醫生。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gǎnmào le, yīnggāi qù kàn yīshēng.

passage.title: 捷運上的要求
passage.hanzi: 在台北搭捷運，有一件事一定要記得：車上不能吃東西，也不能喝飲料。有朋友問我，只喝水可以嗎？當然不行。這是捷運公司的要求，每個人都必須做到。我第一次聽到的時候有點不懂，現在我很喜歡這個要求，因為車上真的很安靜、很舒服。
passage.gloss: When you take the MRT in Taipei, there's one thing you absolutely must remember: you can't eat on the train, and you can't drink beverages either. A friend asked me, is just drinking water OK? Of course not. This is the MRT company's rule, and everyone has to follow it. The first time I heard it I didn't quite get it, but now I really like this rule, because the trains are truly quiet and comfortable.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò, wǒ qù mǎi yǐnliào.
example.gloss: You sit down first, I'll go buy drinks.

grammar.title: 先…才…: A must happen before B
grammar.pattern: Subject + 先 + V1 + ,(然後) + 才 + V2
grammar.explanation: 先 marks the first action and 才 marks the action that can only happen after it. 才 goes right before the second verb, never at the end, and the 才-clause takes no 了. Use this pattern when the first step is a condition for the second: 'only after A, then B'.
grammar.contrast: 先…再… is the neutral way to say 'first A, then B' (simple order, often a plan or suggestion: 我們先吃飯,再去看電影). 先…才… adds the feeling that B is impossible or late without A (要先刷卡才能進去). If you are just listing steps, use 再; if A is a requirement, use 才.
grammar.common_error: Learners put 了 in the first clause and treat 才 like 就 or 然後: 我先吃飯了才去 is wrong. Also they often say 我先做完課才 or leave 才 at the end of the sentence. Keep it as 先 + V1,才 + V2, with no 了 after the 才 verb.

examples.hanzi: 我們先吃飯,才去看電影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān chī fàn, cái qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.gloss: We'll eat first, and only then go see the movie.

examples.hanzi: 你要先讀完書才能玩電腦。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào xiān dú wán shū cái néng wán diànnǎo.
examples.gloss: You have to finish studying before you can play on the computer.

examples.hanzi: 搭捷運要先刷卡才能進去。
examples.pinyin: Dā jiéyùn yào xiān shuā kǎ cái néng jìnqù.
examples.gloss: To take the MRT you have to swipe your card before you can get in.

dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn hěn máng, chángcháng wǎnshàng jiǔ diǎn cái huí jiā.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 太累了吧!以前你都六點就下班。
dialogue.pinyin: Tài lèi le ba! Yǐqián nǐ dōu liù diǎn jiù xiàbān.
dialogue.gloss: That's too tiring! You used to get off work at six.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 對啊,今天又要加班。我先走了喔。
dialogue.pinyin: Duì a, jīntiān yòu yào jiābān. Wǒ xiān zǒu le ō.
dialogue.gloss: Yeah, and today I have to work late again. I'm heading off first.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 好,下班以後打電話給我,我們去吃麵。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo, xiàbān yǐhòu dǎ diànhuà gěi wǒ, wǒmen qù chī miàn.
dialogue.gloss: OK, call me after work and we'll go eat noodles.

sentences.gloss: We'll eat first and only then go stroll the night market.

passage.title: 我的早上
passage.hanzi: 我以前一直不喜歡早起,常常十點才起床,起來又慢慢吃早餐。最近我開始運動,每天早上先去跑步,回家以後才吃早餐。我發現這樣一天的時間長了很多,身體也比以前舒服。以後我還想學游泳。
passage.gloss: I never used to like getting up early. I often wouldn't get out of bed until ten, and then I'd eat breakfast slowly. Recently I started exercising: every morning I go running first, and only after I get home do I eat breakfast. I've found that this way the day feels much longer, and my body feels better than before. In the future I also want to learn to swim.
